phase1DeferredReviews.whyCurrentDslCannotExpressIt: The core r185 behavior evolves two RGBA32Float position/velocity ping-pong pairs in DSL compute and then reads the current pair from the only Scene entity. Under the mandatory component-only rule, those mutable resources must belong to the Scene RenderSet. The frozen TextureComponent creates sampled CopyDst textures and exposes only get(), while BufferComponent exposes only value-returning get()/getRaw() to shaders. Neither component can be written by DSL compute, adopt an externally created mutable resource, or switch an entity slot between ping-pong outputs. Standalone RWTexture2D or RWStructuredBuffer resources would bypass the required RenderSet component ownership, and CPU simulation or per-frame readback would move GPU behavior into C++. Therefore current DSL plus RenderSet cannot preserve the example's core semantics without a public capability expansion.
phase1DeferredReviews.minimumFutureApi: Add a RenderSet-owned mutable GPU component contract. The minimum texture form must declare StorageBinding plus TextureBinding usage, expose typed DSL compute read/write, let one entity select the current resource from a fixed bounded ping-pong bank, publish identical Legacy and UGLIR/MSL/direct-SPIR-V ABI, and retain existing safe out-of-range behavior. An alternative public RW BufferComponent accessor is sufficient only if it supplies the same entity-relative writable indexing and cross-pass synchronization. notes: The DSL and RHI both expose a generic LineStrip topology enum and lower it to Metal and Vulkan. This deferral does not claim that line topology is absent.

The example core is native directed LineStrip rasterization with antialiasing. The Phase 1 normalization rule requires its Scene line geometry to be expanded to triangle-list data; that expansion preserves the centerline interior but not native start-owned/end-excluded endpoint sample ownership and endpoint quantization.

The fixed-sample Chrome/ANGLE Metal probe covered ten slopes and sixteen endpoint phases. Native LineStrip and axis-aligned triangle expansion differed only in paired start/end endpoint samples for the center sample; reversing the directed endpoints changed 160 mask samples. A fixed sample-position translation still left 40 endpoint mask differences.

At the global 400x250 gate, the best normalized triangle implementation passed the initial frame with ratio 0.00057, MAE 0.46705, P99 12, and SSIM 0.99824295. The fixed nonzero frame passed MAE 0.7076, P99 16, and SSIM 0.99752133 but failed the strict differing-pixel ratio at 0.00143. The reproducible diagnostic summary remains build-only at build/custom-lines-raster-probe/summary.json.

TextGeometry produces one logical Line backed by grouped beveled geometry, so the logical Scene still requires exactly one RenderSet under the geometry-groups rule. Loader implementation, geometry volume, dynamic component updates, blending, and private DSL shader translation are all available and are not deferred reasons.

MSAA/resolve expansion, SampleMask, a programmable coverage builtin, and a new public line-rasterization contract are frozen in Phase 1. C++ cannot replace this GPU coverage behavior or issue a direct native-line draw.

phase1DeferredReviews.whyCurrentDslCannotExpressIt: Current UGL DSL and RHI expose a generic LineStrip enum, but the mandated Phase 1 path must normalize the Scene LineStrip to triangle-list data. Existing DSL arithmetic can expand every segment and match its interior, yet it cannot express the native directed start-owned/end-excluded endpoint sample ownership and endpoint quantization used by the fixed four-sample WebGL reference. The current shader surface has no sample-mask or programmable raster-coverage output, the RHI has no deterministic line rasterization/sample-position contract shared by Metal and Vulkan, and Vulkan fixes rasterizationSamples to one. Consequently the triangle-normalized implementation cannot satisfy the same strict Oracle in all four quadrants. Moving coverage to C++ or bypassing the Scene RenderSet with direct draws is prohibited.
phase1DeferredReviews.minimumFutureApi: Define a public deterministic cross-backend native-line sample-coverage contract for DSL/RHI: fixed four-sample positions, directed endpoint ownership, subpixel quantization/tie rules, clipping, and identical Metal/Vulkan behavior while preserving RenderSet indexed-indirect draws. An equivalent programmable sample-coverage output would need the same Legacy and Experimental ABI and backend guarantees. This is a line-rasterization/MSAA/SampleMask capability expansion and remains frozen out of Phase 1; no additional generic LineStrip enum is needed.
phase1DeferredReviews.reentryTest: Re-enable one Scene RenderSet and the private DSL shader after the future coverage contract lands. First run the ten-slope by sixteen-endpoint-phase directed-line probe, including reversed endpoints, and require zero per-sample ownership differences against the pinned r185 WebGL2 reference at the fixed four-sample pattern on both Metal and Vulkan. Then render initial frame 0 and deterministic nonzero frame 60 from the pinned Helvetiker asset and seed 0x18500011 in Legacy and Experimental, three consecutive times per backend. Assert one Set, one instanceCount=1 entity, one indexed-indirect Scene draw, identical component ABI, and all global Oracle plus cross-quadrant thresholds without masks, case-private limits, direct-draw fallback, or C++ GPU work.

notes: The dedicated implementation completes GLB decoding, tangent and helper geometry generation, thirteen one-instance entities in one Scene RenderSet, two material phases, dynamic helper updates, and DSL-only GPU work. Workload, loader work, RenderSet packing, and shader translation are not deferred reasons.

The best single-sample triangle-expanded Legacy/Metal result has initial ratio 0.00958, MAE 0.6548466667, P99 16, and SSIM 0.9814510473; the animated result has ratio 0.01432, MAE 0.96042, P99 21, and SSIM 0.9653997970. Metal and Vulkan outputs are mutually stable, but both differ from the pinned WebGL native-line Oracle at dense one-pixel helper coverage.

Native LineList improves the initial ratio only to approximately 0.00867 and the animated ratio to approximately 0.01032. The remaining mismatch is native directed line endpoint, subpixel quantization, clipping, and sample-coverage behavior, not tunable triangle width. The reproducible reports are build/wave5-probe-webgl-helpers-endpoint/summary.json and build/wave5-probe-webgl-helpers-native/summary.json.

Fragment arithmetic cannot change rasterizer-owned sample coverage, while SampleMask, programmable coverage, sample positions, MSAA/resolve, and a new line-rasterization contract are frozen out of Phase 1. C++ rasterization or direct native draws would violate the GPU and RenderSet boundaries.
